findings.title: Working-hours check compares start to itself and inverts the logic
Date override comparison uses object identity and a questionable offset sign
Override offset logic in getSlots is wrong when the offset crosses a day boundary

response:
## 1) Severity: HIGH | Type: Bug
Title: Working-hours check compares start to itself and inverts the logic

Affected:
- packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:137-151

Explanation:
`end` is computed from `slotStartTime` (a copy-paste error), so it never accounts for the event length. The `find` callback returns true when the slot is outside a single working-hour entry, and that makes the slot unavailable. A user with several working-hour entries on one day, for example 9-12 and 14-17, would have every slot rejected because each slot falls outside at least one of the entries. Working hours are also stored in the organizer's timezone, but the slot is compared in UTC with no conversion. This is wrong for any non-UTC organizer and can wrongly drop valid slots. The fix is to check that the slot lies inside at least one working-hour entry (`some`), using slot end = start + eventLength and converting to the organizer timezone.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
const local = time.tz(organizerTimeZone);
const start = local.hour()*60 + local.minute();
const end = start + eventLength;
const inWorking = workingHours.some(w => w.days.includes(local.day()) && start >= w.startTime && end <= w.endTime);
if (workingHours.length && !inWorking) return false;
~~~

## 2) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Date override comparison uses object identity and a questionable offset sign

Affected:
- packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:105-131

Explanation:
Line 114 compares two dayjs objects with `===`, which is always false, so the intended "zero-length override means unavailable" case is dead code. `dayjs.tz(date.start, tz).utcOffset() * -1` adds the negated offset, and the sign is inconsistent with the conversion in slots.ts, which uses invitee minus organizer offset. `dayjs.tz(date, tz)` also reinterprets the date's wall time in that zone rather than converting it. The `find` is used only for its side effects. The check also runs only against the slot start date, so overrides crossing midnight are mishandled. Because `dateOverrideExist` is set on any matching date, the function returns true early and skips the busy-time check below. A slot inside an override is therefore treated as available even when the host has a conflicting booking.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
// use .isSame()/valueOf() for comparisons, convert with dayjs(date).tz(tz)
// and do not return true early; fall through to the busy check
~~~

## 3) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Override offset logic in getSlots is wrong when the offset crosses a day boundary

Affected:
- packages/lib/slots.ts:211-225

Explanation:
The override start and end times are shifted by the offset between the invitee and organizer timezones, then reduced to minutes of the UTC day. A shift across midnight wraps the hour and can make `endTime < startTime`, or can place the override on the wrong day. `override.start.toString()` is also passed through `dayjs` for no reason and can be parsed in the local timezone. `override.timeZone` may be undefined, and `.tz(undefined)` then silently uses the local zone. The shifted value is computed twice per field.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
const s = dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute");
const e = dayjs(override.end).utc().add(offset, "minute");
// guard timeZone fallback and handle day wrap
~~~
